question:
Arrange the following famous modern Indian paintings in chronological order of their creation:

 
• "Bharat Mata" by Abanindranath Tagore
 
• "Shakuntala" by Raja Ravi Varma
 
• "Three Pujarins" by Jamini Roy
 
• "Mahishasura" by Tyeb Mehta
solution:
**The correct chronological order of creation is:**

 
• **"Shakuntala" by Raja Ravi Varma (1870)**
 
• **"Bharat Mata" by Abanindranath Tagore (1905)**
 
• **"Three Pujarins" by Jamini Roy (1920s-1930s)**
 
• **"Mahishasura" by Tyeb Mehta (1997)**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Shakuntala" by Raja Ravi Varma (1870):**

 
 
• Raja Ravi Varma was one of the most celebrated Indian painters. His painting "Shakuntala" depicts the character from the Mahabharata looking for Dushyanta while pretending to remove a thorn from her foot.
 
 
 
• **"Bharat Mata" by Abanindranath Tagore (1905):**
 
 
• This iconic painting symbolizes Mother India as a calm and composed goddess-like figure, holding a book, sheaves of paddy, a piece of white cloth, and a garland, representing a combination of learning, nourishment, clothing, and devotion.
 
 
 
• **"Three Pujarins" by Jamini Roy (1920s-1930s):**
 
 
• Jamini Roy was an Indian painter who was influenced by the simplification of forms in traditional Indian art. "Three Pujarins" showcases his shift from Western-influenced academic style to traditional Indian folk art.
 
 
 
• **"Mahishasura" by Tyeb Mehta (1997):**
 
 
• Tyeb Mehta was a prominent figure in modern Indian art known for his bold and expressionist style. "Mahishasura" is one of his most famous works depicting the Hindu mythological character in a contemporary style.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ravi Varma**

 
 
• He is often credited with a style that marries European techniques with Indian sensibilities, bringing mythological paintings to the masses.
 
 
 
• **Abanindranath Tagore**
 
 
• As a key figure in the Bengal School of Art, his works often emphasize nationalistic themes and traditional Indian aesthetics.
 
 
 
• **Jamini Roy**
 
 
• His paintings are characterized by bold lines and vibrant colors, often depicting themes from the Ramayana and village life.
 
 
 
• **Tyeb Mehta**
 
 
• He is known for his exploration of the human condition and inner turmoil, often using dramatic contrasts and dynamic compositions.
